answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a time-vested collateral stake before it can transact, with the stake slashed on verified fraud. New identities start at the bottom of a reputation trellis, where trust grows only through a slow history of honest, attested work; a gale of cheap fake accounts cannot rush that climb because stake and time cannot be forged. The zenith of standing, full trading privileges, is reached only after sustained good behavior, so an attacker's cost multiplies with every identity they spin up while their expected payoff collapses.
